items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: not a Reverend Gensel, because he just passed

ctx.x: We need some support in dealing.

Some kind of support system, in the musical — among musicians — so that they can say well I can call, not a Reverend Gensel, because he just passed, but I mean a group of people that have been there, that have decided how they managed that, how they came away from it with grace, and how to maintain your personage. And that’s the one thing I find the saddest thing, that I’ve seen, as long as I’ve been playing. Forty years I’ve been playing. And that’s the saddest thing. When you see them quit. “Oh I’m not playing…

Do you think it sometimes comes from knowing how to deal with perhaps the diminishing physical skill at what they do? Like let’s say a trumpet player has made his mark as a high note man, right? And it gets to the point where they can’t quite get up to © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
